study_identification_part.si4_title: Developmental trajectories of neuroanatomical alterations associated with the 16p11.2 Copy Number Variations

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract explicitly states the aim to characterize age-related effects of 16p11.2 copy number variants using a broad age range and a large normative developmental dataset to adjust for age, fulfilling both the statement of objectives and description of the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: “In this study, we aim at characterizing age-related effects of 16p11.2 copy number variants by analyzing a group with a broad age range including younger individuals. A large normative developmental dataset was used to accurately adjust for effects of age.”

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort (NIHPD) is described with age range, sample size, and that only scans passing quality control were included, but detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria and image quality standards beyond QC and the specific reasons for exclusions are not provided.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the multi-site longitudinal data from Objective 1 … of the publicly available NIHPD project… The normative model … used data from 339 children … for a total of 874 scans. Only subjects that passed quality control were included.”

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are modeled in the mixed-effects normative model, scanner/site effects were tested, and additional linear corrections were applied to account for protocol differences between NIHPD and study scans, indicating explicit handling of key covariates and site effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: “Mixed-effect models were used… we included both linear and quadratic effects of age… Linear effect of sex was also included… During model selection, a fixed effect for individual scanner was tested but found to be not significant…”; “We estimated a linear model … to adjust the 16p11.2 control dataset… The same adjustment was applied to the CNV carrier groups.”

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The normative data source is clearly identified as the publicly available NIHPD project with details on cohort composition and scanning timeline.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the multi-site longitudinal data from Objective 1 … of the publicly available NIHPD project (Evans and Brain Development Cooperative, 2006).”

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The normative model relies on secondary data (the existing NIHPD dataset); per guidance, acquisition protocol reporting for secondary datasets is not applicable.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The preprocessing pipeline is detailed, including denoising, bias correction (N3), intensity normalization, linear and nonlinear registration, brain extraction (BEaST), and use of ANIMAL for registration, covering software and steps.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: “The preprocessing steps applied to the native T1w images were (1) denoising, (2) intensity inhomogeneity correction using the N3 algorithm … (3) intensity normalization by histogram matching to the ICBM152 template… Brain extraction was achieved using the Brain Extraction based on nonlocal Segmentation Technique (BEaST)… images were non-linearly registered using the Automated Nonlinear Image Matching and Anatomical Labelling (ANIMAL) algorithm.”

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study fits the mixed-effects normative model on the NIHPD data but does not describe any data partitioning, cross-validation, or hold-out testing for internal validation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The methods describe modeling age and sex effects on the NIHPD dataset and applying corrections, but no hold-out sets or cross-validation are mentioned.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model derived from NIHPD data was applied directly to the 16p11.2 case-control sample; no independent external healthy dataset was used for validation.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “Data was analyzed for 56 DEL, 19 DUP, 105 familial and unrelated CTRL with ages ranging from 4.5 to 23 years.” (no additional external healthy cohort beyond NIHPD reference and study controls)

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The normative modeling approach is fully described: mixed-effects models with linear and quadratic age terms and sex, formula provided, with implementation details including software (R 3.4.0, nlme).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: “Mixed-effect models were used… we included both linear and quadratic effects of age… Linear effect of sex was also included…”; “The mixed-effects model that best fits the normative data is: Vol i = β0 + γ0 + (β1 + γ1)(Age i -13) + β2(Age i -13)^2 + β3 Sex i + ε i”; “All analyses were conducted using R 3.4.0… The mixed-effect models were built using the nlme package.”

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper describes the modeling approach and subsequent group comparisons but does not report quantitative performance metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage) for the normative model on the reference cohort.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Methods and results detail model specification and group Z-score comparisons but do not provide any numerical fit or calibration metrics for the normative model.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning (training/validation/test) was used when fitting the normative model; therefore reporting characteristics per partition is not applicable.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and package versions are given (R 3.4.0, nlme), and data access notes are provided for the NIHPD and Simons VIP datasets, but there is no mention of code or trained model availability.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: “All analyses were conducted using R 3.4.0… The mixed-effect models were built using the nlme package.”; “Approved researchers can obtain the Simons VIP population dataset described in this study by applying at https://base.sfari.org.”

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohort inclusion is defined by genetic status (16p11.2 deletion/duplication) and age range 4.5–23 years from two consortia, with controls specified and a visual motion QC noted; sample sizes are reported, but detailed exclusion reasons and imaging quality thresholds beyond visual QC are not fully described.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “Cross-sectional data was acquired in 2 different cohorts… we only included participants between 4.5 and 23 years of age. This included 56… deletion carriers… 19 duplication carriers… and 105 controls… The controls were recruited among non-carriers… Because our analysis covers a broad age range… We performed a thorough visual quality control check looking for evidence of motion artefacts.”

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses include age, sex, and genetic group but do not report consideration of clinical covariates such as medication status, symptom severity, or illness duration in deviation score analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: “We used a linear model introducing genetic status as a covariate… The following interaction terms were tested: age*sex and age*group.”

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical data sources are specified as the European 16p11.2 consortium and the Simons VIP study, indicating multi-site origins.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “Cross-sectional data was acquired in 2 different cohorts (the European -EU 16p11.2 consortium and the Simons VIP -SVIP study in North America).”

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes, age distributions, sex ratios, NVIQ means, and ancestry are summarized in Table 1, and psychiatric diagnoses counts are provided in Supplementary Table 1, covering demographic and clinical characteristics.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: “Population characteristics of the 16p11.2 dataset.” (Table with N, age range/mean, sex, scan parameters, NVIQ, ancestry); “A total of 53 of 56 deletion carriers (95%) had at least one psychiatric diagnosis… 15 of 19 duplication carriers (79%) had at least one psychiatric diagnosis…”

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Psychiatric diagnoses are reported with reference to DSM-5 criteria, indicating the diagnostic standard, but specific assessment tools or procedures and measures such as NVIQ instruments are not detailed.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: “From the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, DSM-5 (American Psychiatric Association, 2013).”

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The methods explain the sign of log-Jacobian and Z-scores (negative indicating shrinkage, positive enlargement) and results interpret mean Z-scores for group differences, but no explicit clinical thresholds or categories for deviation scores are provided.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: “A log-transformed Jacobian determinant value less than 0 represents shrinking… a value of 0 indicates that there is no volume change… more than 0 indicates enlargement with respect to the template.”; “Deletion carriers have higher volume than controls… (mean Z-score = 1.165…) Duplication carriers show the opposite effect…”
